media_work.title: The Central Park Five
media_work.focus_or_theme: Wrongful conviction, coerced false confessions, juvenile suspects, racial bias, media frenzy, DNA exoneration.
media_work.summaryNotes: Landmark case exposing issues with juvenile interrogations and false confessions.

media_item.focus_or_theme: Wrongful conviction, coerced false confessions, juvenile suspects, racial bias, media frenzy, DNA exoneration.

research_notes_other.notes_from_film_list.txt: Directed by Ken Burns, Sarah Burns, David McMahon; Examines the 1989 case of five Black and Latino teenagers wrongfully convicted. Available via PBS, Amazon, DVD.
research_notes_other.research_findings: This documentary provides a detailed account of the wrongful conviction of five teenagers in the high-profile "Central Park Jogger" case. It highlights the intense pressure, coercive interrogation tactics, and racial undertones that led to false confessions and convictions despite a lack of physical evidence connecting them. Their exoneration came years later when the actual perpetrator confessed and DNA confirmed his guilt. The case became a symbol of systemic flaws in the justice system, particularly regarding treatment of minority youth and reliance on confessions. Searches did not return specific production company details.

featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: Assault, Rape, Robbery (related to attack on Trisha Meili)
featured_individuals.sentence: Varied, from 5-10 to 5-15 years (Korey Wise, tried as adult, received 5-15)
contributing_factors_raw: Coerced false confessions (obtained after lengthy interrogations without adequate counsel/parental presence), police misconduct, prosecutorial misconduct, racial bias, intense media pressure creating public frenzy.
featured_individuals.status_raw: Exonerated (Convictions vacated after Matias Reyes confessed and DNA confirmed his sole involvement); Received settlement from NYC.
organizations_involved_raw: Innocence Project (involved in later stages/advocacy); Legal teams representing the five.
